historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle volume growth (Energy Storage +5% tapering to +3%, Specialties +3%), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (17.0%) exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR (10.4%) by more than 30% relative and has the opposite sign to the revenue 3yr CAGR (-11.1%). Neither is a usable forward rate: book value was inflated by $4.5B of 2022-23 boom retained earnings and the $2.3B March-2024 preferred raise, then cut by $1.4B of 2024-25 write-offs; revenue went 3.1B -> 9.6B -> 5.1B on the lithium price alone. EPS CAGRs are null because FY2025 EPS is negative (-$5.76) and FY2020-22 straddle the boom.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2022 $602.4M -> FY2025 $644.9M = +2.3%/yr, which is coincidental (FY2022 was a boom-capex year at $1.26B capex, FY2025 a trough-price year at $590M capex). FY2020 owner FCF was -$79.5M so the 5-year CAGR is undefined. Owner FCF ran 7% below reported FCF in FY2025 (SBC 0.9% of revenue) - SBC is small here; the growth story is lithium price x volume, not comp dilution.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle lithium at ~$15/kg LCE from FY2027, volume-led growth of 5% tapering to 3%, 33% adjusted EBITDA margin held flat, capex normalising to ~10% of revenue against 11% D&A. The axes are (1) where the lithium price settles once the 2026 rebound meets 2027 supply, (2) whether Wodgina/Talison/Kings Mountain volumes grow mid-single-digit, (3) whether the $400M cost programme holds the ex-Ketjen margin near 33% at that price. FY2026E owner FCF of ~$1.42B is NOT the base; FY2027 base owner FCF is ~$1.1B and the cyclically elevated FY2026 print is explicitly normalised away.
scenario_narratives.bull: 2027-28 supply deficit holds realised pricing near $20/kg, margins 38-40%, volume +7-8% as Kings Mountain and a Kemerton restart add tonnes; growth capex rises to 11% of revenue to fund it. Requires the deficit thesis AND disciplined capital allocation - the company's 2021-23 record (stranded Kemerton trains) is the reason this is weighted below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: Renewed oversupply returns lithium to ~$10/kg for 2027-28 (the company's own low scenario: ~$4.2B sales, ~$0.95B EBITDA), with a slow drift to ~27% margins by 2032. Balance sheet is not at risk - the downside is a decade of sub-WACC returns on a diluted share count, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Albemarle on a mid-cycle owner-FCF basis, not on the FY2026 price-driven spike or the FY2024-25 trough. The business is a low-cost converter of owned lithium and bromine resources whose earnings are set by an external index price management does not control; the FY2026 guidance table ($0.9B to $4.4B of EBITDA across $10-30/kg) is the honest statement of that. The scenarios map directly onto that table (bear ~$10, base ~$15, bull ~$20) and carry the cyclicality; the discount rate is a plain market-beta WACC with no stacked commodity premium. The share count is the post-conversion 139.6M: the preferred converts in four months and treating it as anything but common would flatter per-share value by ~15%. Specialties (bromine) is the steadier ~$360M EBITDA ballast under the lithium swing.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lithium price path: every $1/kg of sustained realised price is ~$155M of EBITDA (~$0.8/share of annual owner FCF after tax); the base assumes $15/kg mid-cycle, which is a judgment on marginal supply cost, not an observable

Mandatory convertible conversion rate: 21.0M shares at the max rate; if the 20-day VWAP before 1-Mar-2027 exceeds $131 the count falls to 17.5M (+~3% per-share value) - the max rate is the conservative and currently applicable assumption
Windfield cash conversion: 9M-2026 equity income $467M vs $368M dividends received; a persistent gap (JV capex, Australian tax timing) would make adjusted EBITDA overstate distributable cash
Capital allocation: the model assumes capex normalises to ~10% of revenue; a return to 2021-23 build-out intensity (20-30%) without matching volume would consume most of the base-case FCF
NCI valued at $550M (~10x mid-cycle earnings) against $278M book - a ~$2/share judgment either way
China 39% of sales and US EV-policy rollback are demand-side risks inside the bear weight, not separately charged
Terminal value is Gordon-bound in all three scenarios (12.8x base, 13.7x bull, ~12x bear) and ~45-50% of EV; a 1pp move in WACC is worth roughly $10/share

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E: 9M-2026 actual net sales $4,725.1M (Q1 1,428.7 + Q2 1,743.3 + Q3 1,553.1) plus a Q4 estimate of ~$1,375M, management having guided Q4 sales and adjusted EBITDA down sequentially on lower lithium pricing. Sits at the top of the company's ~$20/kg LCE scenario ($5.7-6.0B) because Q1 still carried two months of the divested Refining Solutions business (~$180M).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted on the post-conversion basis: 118.544M weighted diluted shares for Q3 2026 (10-Q EPS note, includes RSU/PSU dilution) + 21.02M common issuable on mandatory conversion of 2,299,769 Series A preferred shares at the MAXIMUM rate of 9.140 common per preferred. The max rate applies because the $99.25 price is below the $109.41 threshold (= $1,000 / 9.140); at or above $131.27 the min rate (7.618) would give 17.52M. Conversion is automatic on ~1-Mar-2027, inside year 1 of the forecast, so the count is treated as already converted and held FLAT thereafter (SBC is expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count). The ~136M in company FY2026 guidance is a weighted-average that only includes the conversion for part of the year and at a different assumed VWAP.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30-Sep-2026 10-Q: total long-term debt $1,881.4M (current portion $74.6M + non-current $1,806.8M) less cash and equivalents $1,846.0M. Down from $3,193.5M debt at 31-Dec-2025 after ~$1.3B of note redemptions funded by the Refining Solutions ($525M net) and Eurecat ($123M) divestitures. Operating lease liabilities (~$100M) are excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost is already inside adjusted EBITDA (treatment B). The $2.3B mandatory convertible preferred is treated as common (see share_count_basis), not as debt.
inputs.fcf_note: FY2026E owner FCF = reported FCF 1,460 - SBC incl. equity-award taxes 37.7 - interest income 0. Reported: 9M-2026 OCF $1,462.0M less capex $250.8M = $1,211.2M, plus a Q4 estimate (OCF ~$330M, capex ~$80M to land inside the $300-350M FY guidance). THIS IS A CYCLICALLY ELEVATED FIGURE at ~$20/kg LCE realised pricing and unusually low capex; it is the FY0 anchor only. The driver paths normalise FY2027 to a mid-cycle price and a sustaining capex level - do not read last_fcf as the base the valuation capitalises. FY2025 actual for reference: reported FCF $692.5M, owner FCF $644.9M at ~$9-10/kg.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement stock-based compensation add-back: 9M-2026 $24.2M (Q1 7.9 + Q2 6.8 + Q3 9.6, 10-Qs) + Q4 estimate $8M = $32.2M; plus cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement 9M-2026 $4.5M + Q4 ~$1M = $5.5M (kpis equity_award_taxes). Albemarle publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 actual: $40.3M + $7.3M = $47.5M (0.92% of revenue); FY2024 $32.1M + $11.9M = $44.0M (0.82%).
inputs.interest_income_note: Net debt is ~$35M on a ~$1.4B owner-FCF base, so there is no net cash pile being added to EV and nothing to double-count. Interest income (inside Other income, net; down $12.5M YoY for 9M-2026 on lower rates, so roughly $40-50M/yr on $1.8B cash) is below the EBITDA line and does not enter the unlevered flows.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2023-FY2025 or 9M-2026 (financing activities). The flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding; the common dividend ($0.41/qtr, ~$190M/yr) is the shareholder return.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:03Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated Sunday 2026-11-08, so this is the latest close
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x ~1.5 beta (ALB's 5-year beta against the S&P 500 runs 1.4-1.7) = ~11.7% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~4.2% on $1.9B of notes; market equity ~$13.9B (139.6M diluted x $99.25) gives ~12% debt weight; blended ~10.8%, used as 10.5% (house US default). The SAME WACC is applied to all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows (bear at ~$10/kg LCE, bull at ~$20/kg), not again through a scenario-specific or ad-hoc commodity premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): operating lease cost is expensed inside adjusted EBITDA under US GAAP (ASC 842), so no separate lease charge in the flows and the ~$100M of lease liabilities is excluded from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is the 50% of Jordan Bromine Company (JBC) held by Arab Potash, consolidated in Specialties. Charged ONCE in the equity bridge, not in the flows: deducted at $550M, about 10x mid-cycle attributable NCI earnings (~$55M/yr: 9M-2026 $49.1M annualises to ~$65M on strong bromine pricing, FY2025 ran ~$44M; dividends to NCI $56.1M 9M-2026). Book NCI is $278.5M at 30-Sep-2026; the premium to book reflects JBC's Dead Sea cost position and is a judgment. The ~$4/share it costs is the price of leaving the consolidated flows intact.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical commodity-chemicals producer) via the Drivers route, routed through dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the owner-fcf-adaptations file read for the cyclical/NCI/matching-asset rules. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. WHY THIS MODEL: Albemarle is a mine-to-chemical converter whose value is a stream of free cash flow; the only adaptation the commodity exposure needs is mid-cycle normalisation of the FY0 anchor, done in the driver paths. EQUITY-METHOD INCOME: ~70% of Energy Storage profit arrives as 'equity in net income of unconsolidated investments' from the 49%-owned Windfield (Talison/Greenbushes) JV - $466.8M for 9M-2026 vs $368.4M of dividends actually received. Adjusted EBITDA includes Windfield's pre-tax share (the company adds back the proportionate Windfield tax), so the EBITDA margin paths below are on that basis, the cash tax path taxes it once, and the Windfield carrying value ($970.6M) is NOT added in the bridge because its income is already in the flows (matching-asset rule). The dividend-vs-equity-income lag is a timing item that reverses over the cycle. WORKING CAPITAL: inventory + receivables exceed payables and the inventory balance moves with the lithium price, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-10% of the revenue change): the FY2027 revenue decline releases cash, later growth consumes it. CAPEX: FY2026's $300-350M is a deferral low (Kemerton idled, early-stage projects resequenced); D&A runs ~$670M. The paths step capex back toward D&A (10% of revenue vs 11%) so the terminal year is not capitalising a sustaining-capex holiday; the residual ~1pp gap is intangible amortisation that needs no reinvestment. DATA CORRECTION: the Analysis JSON describes the preferred as $1.75B; the 10-Q states 2,300,000 shares x $1,000 liquidation preference = $2.3B gross (46M depositary shares at $50), carried at $2,235.1M net of issue costs. Preferred dividends run $41.7M/quarter ($166.8M/yr), with two payments left (1-Dec-2026, 1-Mar-2027) before conversion - deducted in the bridge.

bear.growth_note: FY2027 ~$4.27B, the company's own ~$10/kg scenario ($4.1-4.3B): renewed oversupply from Chinese lepidolite, African hard rock and Argentine brine pushes pricing back to the 2024-25 trough (Rothschild Redburn / UBS bear view). Volume still grows 3-4% but at trough prices; US EV incentive rollback and China tariff friction cap demand.
bear.margin_note: ~$0.98B FY2027 adjusted EBITDA, matching the $10/kg scenario ($0.9-1.0B). Recovers to 27% by 2032 as the $400M cost programme and a drift back to ~$12/kg equivalent pricing take hold - still below the base mid-cycle.
bear.da_note: ~$640M of D&A on a $4.27B base is 15%; the fixed asset base does not shrink with the lithium price.
bear.capex_note: Capex held near maintenance (~$320M FY2027) as in 2024-25; no growth projects sanctioned.
bear.narrative: Oversupply redux: 2027 looks like 2025 - lithium at ~$10/kg, Energy Storage EBITDA under $0.7B, the newly converted 21M preferred shares diluting a trough. ALB survives comfortably (net debt ~zero, $3.4B liquidity, no maturities before Q4-2028) but earns little more than its cost of capital for a decade.

base.growth_note: FY2027 revenue ~$5.25B: realised lithium normalises from ~$20/kg to a ~$15/kg mid-cycle (roughly the marginal cost of integrated hard-rock/lepidolite supply), partly offset by +5% Energy Storage volume (Wodgina ramp, Talison CGP3 back after the June-2026 fire) and +3% Specialties; also drops the ~$180M Q1-2026 Refining Solutions stub. Thereafter volume-led growth: +5% tapering to +3% as ESS/EV demand compounds (management: lithium demand +48% YTD Aug-2026) with flat real pricing.
base.margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA (incl. Windfield pre-tax share) ~$1.73B in FY2027, interpolated from the company's own FY2026 sensitivity ($0.9-1.0B at $10/kg, $2.4-2.6B at $20/kg -> ~$1.7B at $15/kg) plus Specialties at $350-375M. Pre-boom FY2019 adjusted EBITDA margin was ~29% including low-margin Ketjen; ex-Ketjen ~32%, before the $400M/yr cost programme. 33% held flat: no re-rating of the mid-cycle price, no further cost programme credited.
base.da_note: FY2026 guidance $660-680M = ~11% of FY2026E revenue, ~12.5% of the lower FY2027 base; drifts to 11% as revenue grows faster than the asset base.
base.capex_note: FY2027 ~$420M vs the FY2026 deferral low of $300-350M, stepping to ~10% of revenue (~$580M by FY2029) as sustaining spend normalises and Kings Mountain proceeds with DOE/DoD support. Terminal capex 10% vs D&A 11%.
base.tax_note: Cash taxes paid: FY2022 $248M, FY2023 $319M, FY2024 $263M (on a loss - Chile/Australia JV taxes), FY2025 $152M. Albemarle's adjusted ETR has historically been guided at 22-27%; 25% applied to EBIT including the Windfield pre-tax share (which adjusted EBITDA grosses up). Pillar Two is a modest upside risk to the rate.
base.narrative: Mid-cycle: lithium settles at ~$15/kg LCE from 2027 and stays there in real terms; volumes grow mid-single-digit on EV plus grid storage; Specialties compounds at ~3% with ~24% margins. No credit for a 2027-28 supply deficit, no penalty for renewed oversupply.

bull.growth_note: FY2027 ~$5.86B: lithium holds ~$19-20/kg as the 2027-28 supply deficit (industry capex cuts incl. Kemerton, Chinese lepidolite curtailments) materialises; only the Refining Solutions stub drops out. Volume +7-8% in 2028-29 as Kings Mountain and a Kemerton restart add tonnes into a tight market.
bull.margin_note: ~$2.35B FY2027 adjusted EBITDA, inside the company's $20/kg scenario ($2.4-2.6B) after the Ketjen stub. Fades to 38% as spodumene input costs and royalties catch up with price.
bull.capex_note: Growth capex restarts in a tight market: 11% of a larger revenue base (~$900M+/yr by 2030) - the bull case pays for its own volume.
bull.narrative: Supply deficit: 2027-28 lithium tightness keeps realised pricing near $20/kg, the low-cost Greenbushes/Atacama position earns its scarcity premium, and ALB redeploys cash into Kings Mountain and a Kemerton restart at attractive returns. Still well short of the 2022-23 $40-70/kg super-cycle.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 30/45/25. Bear up to 30%: lithium sat at or below $10/kg for most of 2024-25, credible sell-side houses (Rothschild Redburn, UBS) explicitly forecast a 2027 oversupply and EBITDA decline, and ALB's own guidance framework treats $10/kg as a live scenario - this is a recurring state of the world, not a tail. Bull down to 25%: the deficit case needs sustained ~$20/kg pricing AND volume growth AND capital discipline on redeployment, three independent things, and management guided Q4-2026 down sequentially on softening prices. Base 45%: the mid-cycle anchor. No going-concern component in any scenario (net debt ~zero, no maturities before Q4-2028).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
